findings.evidence: `rg -n 'maximal tableau'` hits lines 17, 30, 146, 158, and 215; Mathlib defines `highestWeight_apply` as `if (i,j) ∈ μ then i else 0`, while uniformly increasing in-shape entries gives larger semistandard tableaux.
findings.fix: Replace “maximal tableau” throughout with “highest-weight tableau” or “tableau whose row `i` contains `i`.”
findings.issue: Lines 17, 30, 146, 158, and 215 call `highestWeight μ` the “maximal tableau,” but it is not maximal: tableau entries are unbounded, and the declaration is the row-index/highest-weight tableau.

findings.evidence: Lines 162–164 explain the subset/cardinality proof and lines 184–185 explain how the finiteness proof bounds entries using one tableau.
findings.fix: Retain concise result descriptions and remove the “Indeed…” counting argument and the representative-tableau proof explanation.
findings.issue: The docstrings for `eq_highestWeight_of_content_eq_rowLen` (lines 158–164) and `finite_content_eq` (lines 184–185) narrate their proof arguments rather than only describing the results.

summary: Several docstrings misidentify `highestWeight` as maximal and include proof narration instead of documenting only the result.
